title: Project Overview
description: Start with README.md. It describes eruption-forecast as a Python package that processes raw seismic tremor, extracts time-series features, trains multi-seed classifier ensembles and produces probabilistic volcanic eruption forecasts. It lays out the CalculateTremor-to-ExplanationModel pipeline and the SDS/FDSN data sources that the rest of this tour follows stage by stage. The wiki Home page is the navigation hub for the detailed workflow guides referenced later.

title: Running the Pipeline
description: main.py is the reference end-to-end script: it chains ForecastModel's calculate, train, predict, evaluate and explain stages over a list of known eruption dates. forecast-scenario.py is the second entry point. It runs tremor calculation once, then loops shared training, prediction and evaluation over several Scenario dicts. The Pipeline-Walkthrough wiki page annotates both workflows and shows what each stage contributes.

title: The ForecastModel Orchestrator
description: Every stage in main.py goes through ForecastModel, which chains calculate, train, predict, evaluate and explain and captures each stage's keyword arguments into a hierarchical ForecastConfig. That captured config lets save_config(), from_config() and run() replay a full experiment from a YAML file. ForecastModelScenario wraps one ForecastModel so the expensive tremor calculation runs only once across many scenarios.
languageLesson: Method chaining (a fluent interface) works because each stage method returns self, typed as typing.Self. You can then write fm.calculate(...).train(...).predict(...) as a single expression while the object builds up state.

title: Seismic Data Sources
description: The first stage needs waveforms. SeismicDataSource is an abstract base class with one get(date) method that returns an ObsPy Stream. SDS reads a local SeisComP archive, and FDSN downloads daily data from a web service and caches it transparently in a local SDS archive. Because both share one interface, the tremor stage does not need to know where the data comes from.
languageLesson: Python's abc.ABC with @abstractmethod defines an interface that subclasses must implement. Instantiating a subclass that leaves get() undefined raises TypeError, which catches incomplete data sources early.

title: Calculating Seismic Tremor
description: CalculateTremor pulls the stream for each day from a data source and computes three metrics across frequency bands in parallel. RSAM is the windowed mean amplitude per band, DSAR is the ratio between consecutive bands, and Shannon entropy measures broadband signal complexity. It merges the daily results into a 10-minute tremor CSV, and TremorData wraps that CSV with cached properties so later stages can read it.

title: Building Eruption Labels
description: Supervised learning needs targets. LabelBuilder slides a time window over the date range and marks a window positive (is_erupted=1) when an eruption falls within the next day_to_forecast days. DynamicLabelBuilder builds per-eruption windows in three phases. LabelData wraps the resulting label CSV and parses the window parameters back out of its filename, matching how TremorData wraps the tremor CSV from Step 5.

title: Features from Tremor Windows
description: TremorMatrixBuilder slices the tremor time series from Step 5 into windows aligned with the labels from Step 6 and checks that each window has the expected number of samples. FeaturesBuilder runs tsfresh extraction on each tremor column and caches the results as Parquet. FeatureSelector then keeps only the informative features, using either tsfresh's FDR p-value filter or random-forest permutation importance.

title: BaseModel and Caching
description: Each pipeline stage model inherits from BaseModel. It handles tremor loading, date and directory resolution, and a content-addressable cache: a hash of the stage parameters and a tremor fingerprint names the pickle file, so a repeated run with the same inputs loads from disk instead of recomputing. Each stage also writes its settings to a YAML config through a dataclass that shares stamping and dict round-tripping from BaseConfig.
languageLesson: Content-addressable caching derives the cache key from a hash of the inputs, such as a sorted JSON dump of the parameters. Any change to the parameters produces a different key, so stale results are never reused and no manual invalidation is needed.

title: Multi-Seed Training
description: TrainingModel puts Steps 6 and 7 together. It builds labels, extracts features, then selects features and fits a GridSearchCV classifier for each of many random seeds. ClassifierModel wraps the 11 supported estimators and their hyperparameter grids. utils/ml.py provides the resampling, grid search and model-registry helpers.

title: The Ensemble Stack
description: The per-seed models from Step 9 are stored in two layers. SeedEnsemble is an sklearn-compatible classifier that bundles every seed model for one classifier and returns probabilities with uncertainty. ClassifierEnsemble holds one SeedEnsemble per classifier and computes consensus predictions. BaseEnsemble supplies the shared joblib save and load methods. ClassifierEnsemble is one of the most imported modules in the package, so this stack connects training to the prediction, evaluation and explanation stages.
languageLesson: SeedEnsemble subclasses sklearn's BaseEstimator and ClassifierMixin. Implementing fit, predict and predict_proba with those mixins lets a custom class work with sklearn utilities that expect a standard classifier.

title: Producing Forecasts
description: PredictionModel loads a trained ClassifierEnsemble, builds an unlabelled grid of windows over the forecast period and extracts features the same way as in training. It then computes eruption probability, uncertainty and confidence for each classifier and for the consensus. Its cache key includes the training hash, so retraining automatically invalidates old forecasts. forecast_plots.py draws the probability-over-time figure with eruption markers.

title: Evaluating Ensembles
description: EvaluationModel scores a pre-trained ensemble against ground truth and never refits it. It runs in two modes: training reuse takes labels from the TrainingModel, and prediction reuse rebuilds labels over the forecast grid from known eruption dates. MetricsEnsemble computes probability and prediction matrices with one column per seed, plus aggregate ROC, PR and threshold metrics. ClassifierComparator ranks classifiers against each other.

title: Explaining Predictions with SHAP
description: The last stage asks why the ensemble predicted what it did. ExplanationModel reuses a TrainingModel or PredictionModel, and ExplainerEnsemble runs SHAP TreeExplainer for each seed in parallel. It covers tree classifiers only (RF, lite-rf, GB, XGB) and skips the rest with a warning. The results are stored as SeedExplanation and ClassifierExplanation dataclasses and drawn as bar, beeswarm and per-eruption waterfall plots.
languageLesson: Dataclasses declared with slots=True store their fields in fixed slots instead of a per-instance __dict__. That saves memory when you hold one explanation object per seed across hundreds of seeds.

title: Shared Infrastructure
description: A few modules support every stage above. logger.py, a Loguru wrapper with per-category error logs, and utils/pathutils.py, which handles output directories, figure saving and data I/O, are the two most imported files in the codebase. date_utils.py normalises dates and parses label filenames. The Output-Structure wiki page shows the station-level directory tree for each stage.

title: Architecture Recap
description: Finish with the Architecture guide, which connects the package layout, the BaseModel hierarchy and the ensemble stack covered in this tour. The package __init__.py re-exports the public API (tremor calculation, label and feature builders, stage models and ForecastModel), so it summarises what users are expected to import. Use the API-Reference page for full details of every class you have now seen in context.
